newsitem.title: USA: Advocacy groups try to block plutonium to Canada.
newsitem.headline: Advocacy groups try to block plutonium to Canada.

text.p: Three public interest groups on Friday said they filed a petition with federal regulators to try to stop proposed exports of U.S. military plutonium to Canada to test its use in civilian nuclear reactors.
The Nuclear Control Institute, the Natural Resources Defense Council and Greenpeace petitioned the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission to reject the proposed shipment.

The groups said the export of the bomb material as civilian fuel would harm national security and influence a current federal review of options for disposing of surplus plutonium from the U.S. nuclear arsenal.

In their petition, the groups said the pending license application was for slightly more than 2 pounds (1 kilogram) of plutonium contained in fuel pellets, but said eventually as much as 50 tons (50.8 tonnes) of surplus weapons-grade plutonium could be made available by the United States and Russia for the Canadian civilian reactor program.

"From the non-proliferation interest of limiting to the fullest possible extent commerce in weapons-usable materials, the complete demise of the commercial plutonium industry would be desirable," the groups said in a statement.
